segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The crack ran the whole length of the main beam of the schoolroom, and the sexton put his thumb into it up to the knuckle without difficulty. He said the spring damp had got in above the north gable, and had likely been getting in since before the old rector died. He mentioned twice that he had spoken of it to the rector. Mr Silas Rowe stood under it with his hat in his hand and did not point out that the mention had been made to a man three years in his grave.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Fenner the mason at Bramdean would want fifteen pounds, timber and labour together, and would not begin before he was sure of it. The poor box held four pounds and eleven shillings, of which two were promised to the Ludd family at the mill cottages, whose youngest had been ill since Easter. Eighty a year does not stretch to roofs.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he wrote out a subscription notice in his best hand and carried it up the stairs beside the draper's to the circulating library, where any paper pinned to the door is read by the whole parish within two days. Mrs Hale was below, arguing about buttons. Miss Judith Vane was at the counter, and she looked up at him directly, which she always did, and which he had never learned to like.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Mrs Hale has gone down. I came to change my brother's volume and have been left in charge of the whole of literature.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: said Miss Vane. He explained the beam, and the fifteen pounds, and held out the notice. She read it twice before she answered.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: I will keep the subscription book here, if you like, and enter the sums myself. But I would not pin that up.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: It is plainly written.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: said Rowe.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: It is. Only a notice on a door asks nobody in particular, and nobody in particular gives. Go to Mr Hollis at Nine Acres, who sold his hops very well in March and has waited two months for somebody to notice it. Then Mrs Yardley, who kept a school herself at Alton and will give five pounds to be asked before Hollis is.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Rowe turned his hat round once in his hands. He had been under a broken roof since seven, and doing sums the whole way up the hill.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: That is parish politics, Miss Vane, dressed up as advice.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he said.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: I would rather ask the parish honestly and be refused honestly.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Then you had better ask it. Give me the notice and I will hand it to Mrs Hale, and you may keep your own book.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She took the paper, laid it under the ledger, and turned to the shelf. The offer had been withdrawn so quietly that he was on the stairs before he understood it had been.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was prevented from getting further by Mrs Pike, who came up at the pace of a woman carrying something too good to keep.

segments.speaker: Mrs Honoria Pike
segments.text: Miss Vane. Mr Rowe. The gatehouse at Amberlight House is being aired. Two women scrubbing since Tuesday and beds made up above. It is Miss Louisa Marchmont, the niece, come down a fortnight on the family's business, two-and-twenty, and nobody with her but a maid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mrs Pike sat down upon the one chair the library possessed and looked at the curate with the satisfaction of a woman who has found the lid that fits the pot.

segments.speaker: Mrs Honoria Pike
segments.text: Well. There is your fifteen pounds and a good deal more besides. The black coat will do if the cuffs are seen to, and you must have a new neckcloth, and you are not to wear those buckles. Wednesday. I shall arrange it.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: Madam, I want subscriptions. I do not want a wife.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: said Rowe.

segments.speaker: Mrs Honoria Pike
segments.text: Then you shall have both, and in a twelvemonth you will thank me for the second and have forgotten the first entirely.
